# Project Brief: Research Catalog Database

## 1. Executive Summary
The Research Catalog Database is a full‑stack platform that continuously ingests AI research papers (initially arXiv) and relevant GitHub repositories, applies LLM-driven enrichment (summaries, tags, questions addressed, key findings, qualitative scoring), and maintains a lightweight graph-backed knowledge base to enable similarity discovery, theory exploration, and research clustering. The MVP emphasizes fast ingestion, consistent enrichment, unified search, and an early “theory mode” for exploratory hypothesis validation.

## 2. Problem Statement
Researchers, engineers, and strategy stakeholders struggle to quickly: (a) find cohesive clusters of emerging work, (b) connect publications to implementation code, and (c) evaluate real-world relevance vs. novelty. Existing tools (Connected Papers, Litmaps, PapersWithCode) each cover fragments (citation network visualization, trending, code links) but lack unified theory/question exploration with an explainable scoring model across both papers and code repositories in near-real time.

## 3. Target Users & Ranked Priorities
1. Applied ML Researchers / Research Engineers
2. Product / Strategy Analysts (AI strategy, competitive intelligence)
3. Advanced Students / Academics exploring topic landscapes
4. Technical Investors / Advisors (early signal scanning)
5. Tool Builders (embedding / evaluation frameworks)

## 4. Core Jobs To Be Done (JTBD)
- Rapidly surface the most relevant & novel papers for a topic / theory.
- Discover implementation repositories tied to conceptual advances.
- Explore clusters of semantically and thematically similar work.
- Validate or challenge a theory (support vs. contradict counts & rationale).
- Input a single paper or repo URL and get enriched metadata + similar items.

## 5. MVP Feature Scope
Included:
- Continuous ingestion: arXiv papers (categories: cs.AI, cs.LG, stat.ML initially) every 30 min.
- GitHub repo discovery: keyword & topic search + stars/recency heuristic (20 candidates/day target).
- LLM enrichment pipeline (OpenAI / Azure OpenAI): summary, tags, questions answered, key findings, two scores (Real-World Relevance, Interestingness) 1–10.
- Lightweight graph model atop TinyDB (JSON) + adjacency / semantic edge overlay.
- Unified search (papers + repos) with relevance ranking (embedding similarity + score composite).
- Theory Mode: user supplies theory/question → system aggregates supporting/contradicting evidence.
- Sparse result fallback: suggest related theories OR trigger deeper ingestion cycle.
- Single URL analysis (paper PDF or repo) on demand.

Deferred / Stretch (Not MVP):
- Alerting / subscriptions.
- Full citation network ingestion.
- Time trend visualizations.
- Export (CSV/JSON datasets).
- Interactive embedding playground.
- Advanced UI visual graph (initial: simple cluster facets only).

## 6. Non-Goals (MVP)
- Full PDF OCR for scanned documents.
- Exhaustive multi-source coverage (only arXiv + GitHub starting).
- Full deduplicated global citation metrics (approximate citation count optional if cheaply available).

## 7. Key Differentiators
- Theory-driven querying (support vs oppose) unified across papers & repos.
- Dual qualitative scoring with transparent rationale metadata.
- Graph + semantic hybrid built on a minimal local store (no managed DB needed for POC).
- Early linking of paper → repo (bidirectional edges with confidence source).

## 8. Data & Ingestion Strategy
- Paper Source: arXiv API (poll every 30 min; maintain last updated timestamp). Pagination & category filters.
- Repo Source: GitHub REST/GraphQL (search queries combining keywords extracted from recent papers + curated seed topics). Rate-limit respectful.
- Ingestion Queue: Simple priority queue (papers first, then repos) with concurrency limit (e.g., 3 workers) to avoid API burst.
- Retry & Backoff: Exponential for transient HTTP errors (max 3 attempts then mark stale).
- Deduplication: Hash (source_id + version for arXiv), repo full_name for GitHub.
- Raw Storage: PDFs saved under `data/papers/{arxiv_id}.pdf` (optional: toggle to skip PDF to reduce disk). Repos optionally shallow-cloned (`data/repos/{owner}__{name}`) for structure sampling.

## 9. Knowledge Model (Initial Entities & Relationships)
Entities:
- Paper(id, title, authors, abstract, published_at, categories, pdf_path, summary, tags[], questions[], findings[], scores{relevance, interesting}, embedding_ref, rationale_meta)
- Repo(id, full_name, stars, topics[], readme_excerpt, summary, tags[], questions[], findings[], scores{relevance, interesting}, embedding_ref, rationale_meta)
- Theory(id, text, created_at)
- Topic (derived tag/topic aggregator)

Edges (typed):
- PAPER_SIMILAR_TO_PAPER (semantic cosine + threshold)  
- REPO_SIMILAR_TO_REPO  
- PAPER_IMPL_BY_REPO (inferred if repo mentions paper id/title/keywords)  
- SUPPORTS_THEORY / CONTRADICTS_THEORY / RELATED_TO_THEORY  
- HAS_TOPIC (entity → topic)  

Storage Implementation:
- Base: TinyDB collections per entity type.
- Graph Overlay: Separate JSON edge list with forward/back adjacency indexes.
- Embeddings: Local `embeddings/` directory mapping content hash → vector (pickle or NumPy `.npy`).

## 10. Similarity & Ranking Approach
Embedding Model: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` (fallback: `text-embedding-3-small` if cost override).  
Similarity Score: 0.55 * cosine + 0.20 * topical overlap Jaccard + 0.15 * recency decay + 0.10 * interestingness normalized.  
Clustering (MVP): Periodic (every 4 hours) mini-batch HDBSCAN OR (simpler fallback) k-means (k adaptive via sqrt(n/2)).  
Store cluster labels; expose cluster facet in search.

## 11. LLM Enrichment
Pipeline Steps Per Item:
1. Extract raw text (paper: abstract + optionally intro; repo: README + top-level file names + short code sample heuristics).  
2. Summarize (prompt tuned for concise structured YAML/JSON).  
3. Generate: tags, questions answered, key findings bullet list.  
4. Score rubric prompt: relevance (practical impact + applicability) & interestingness (novelty + surprise).  
5. Produce rationale snippet (max 400 chars) for each score.  
Prompt Reuse: deterministic template with few-shot examples (saved under `prompts/`).  
Cost Control: batch embedding calls; early skip embedding if item lacks substantive text length threshold.

## 12. Operational & Performance Targets (MVP)
- Avg ingestion + enrichment latency ≤ 3 min per item (95th ≤ 7 min).
- Daily capacity target: 200 papers, 20 repos (scalable by adjusting interval).
- Storage footprint: < 2 GB first week (assuming limited PDF retention optional toggle).
- Embedding cache hit rate after first week: > 85% on reprocessing.

## 13. Scores & Heuristics Details
Relevance Score Inputs: topical alignment to high-level applied categories (LLM tags vs. curated list), presence of benchmark results, mentions of deployment context.  
Interestingness Score Inputs: novelty language signals ("first", "novel", "we propose"), divergence in embedding from centroid of cluster, unusual tag combination frequency.  
Normalization: z-score within rolling 7‑day window then scaled to 1–10.

## 14. Frontend Experience (Initial)
Design: Minimal research console with dark mode default.  
Pages:
- Dashboard: ingestion status + recent clusters.
- Search: unified multi-entity results (chips: Paper/Repo/Theory, cluster facet, tag filters).
- Item Detail: enriched metadata, scores, similar items panel.
- Theory Explorer: input box → support vs contradict table + suggestions.
- Admin/Settings: toggle ingestion, adjust polling interval, cost dashboard.  
UI Stack: Vite + React + Tailwind (if allowed) or minimal custom CSS; component-first design for future expansion.

## 15. API & Backend Outline
- Service Layers:
  - Ingestion Scheduler (async tasks; could use `asyncio` loops or lightweight APScheduler).
  - Fetchers: arXivFetcher, GitHubRepoFetcher.
  - EnrichmentWorker: orchestrates LLM calls & embedding generation.
  - GraphService: similarity index + edge maintenance.
  - SearchService: vector search (naive in-memory Faiss optional future; MVP pure cosine on loaded vectors).
  - TheoryService: hypothesis indexing & evidence aggregation.
- API (FastAPI): endpoints for search, item detail, theory analysis, ingestion control, health, cluster listing.

## 16. Tech Stack Decisions (MVP)
- Python: FastAPI + uvicorn.
- Task Concurrency: `asyncio` tasks (avoid Celery/Kafka complexity for MVP).
- Storage: TinyDB + flat files (embeddings, PDFs, repos).
- Embeddings & LLM: OpenAI / Azure OpenAI (config via `.env`).
- Testing: Pytest (backend), Playwright for frontend E2E (later stage after initial UI skeleton).
- Containerization: Dockerfile (multi-stage: builder + runtime).  

## 17. Security & Compliance (MVP)
- No PII collected.  
- API keys in `.env` (never commit).  
- Rate limit external API calls; exponential backoff.  
- Basic auth or API key gate for control endpoints (toggle ingestion) (stretch if time).  

## 18. Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|------------|
| High LLM cost scaling | Budget overrun | Medium | Batch embeddings, early text length filter, cost dashboard |
| Sparse theory evidence | Low trust | Medium | Suggest related theories + trigger targeted ingestion burst |
| Low-quality tags | Reduced search precision | Medium | Add post-tag LLM refinement or frequency pruning |
| Graph drift / stale clusters | Misleading clusters | Medium | Re-cluster every 4 hours + recalc edges diff |
| Rate limits (GitHub/arXiv) | Ingestion stalls | Low-Med | Backoff + persist last cursor + jitter intervals |
| Hallucinated findings | Misinterpretation | Medium | Restrictive prompt + require source snippet grounding |
| Disk growth (PDFs/repos) | Resource pressure | Low | Configurable retention policy + periodic prune |

## 19. Success Metrics (Initial)
- M1: ≥ 2,000 enriched items discoverable with < 300 ms median search response.
- Retrieval Relevance (internal eval set): MRR ≥ 0.55 baseline.
- Average end-to-end enrichment latency ≤ 3 min.
- User theory query: ≥ 70% yield non-empty support/contradict set within first week corpus.

## 20. Open Questions / Assumptions
Assumptions (can revise in PRD):
- GitHub topic search + curated keywords sufficient for MVP repository discovery.
- No need for full citation graph initially; embedding similarity acceptable proxy.
- Single embedding model adequate (no hybrid lexical index in MVP).
- TinyDB performance OK up to ~10–15K items before refactor.

Resolved Questions (user provided answers):
1. Lightweight lexical fallback day 1? → No (defer; rely solely on embedding + tag filtering).  
2. User accounts & personalization early? → No (keep single-tenant stateless UI).  
3. Ingestion expansion aggressiveness? → Only expand categories on explicit user demand (add a configurable allow-list).  
4. On-prem / air-gapped requirement? → No (optimize for cloud/OpenAI integration; no abstraction layer required yet).  

Remaining Open (carry to PRD for optional refinement):
- Whether to add approximate nearest neighbor lib (Faiss / hnswlib) before 10K items.
- Policy for pruning or archiving stale repos (no commits > N months).
- Threshold rules for auto-triggering targeted ingestion when theory coverage is sparse.
